passages.original: Hoc vero opus hodie in quinque partes, ut ab auctore exierat, distributum Labetur. Ille autem ad centum quinquaginta tres illos pisces quos apostoli, post Christi resurrectionem, uno retis s jactu cepisse referuntur in Evangelio (Joan. XXI, 11), alludens, sub centum quinquaginta tribus tilulis (ut uotavit Cassiodorus) omnes Christi Domini promissiones, per totum Scripturæ sacrae campum diffusas, voluit contineri : quas ideo ille in unum collegit, ut eas vere a Christo fuisse impletas, aut in posterum certo certius implendas fore demonstraret.
passages.english: This work, however, is today held divided into five parts, as it had come from its author. He, alluding to those one hundred and fifty-three fish which the apostles, after Christ's resurrection, are reported in the Gospel (John 21:11) to have caught with a single cast of the net, wished all the promises of Christ the Lord, scattered over the whole field of sacred Scripture, to be contained under one hundred and fifty-three headings (as Cassiodorus noted). He gathered them into one for this reason: to show that they had truly been fulfilled by Christ, or would most certainly be fulfilled in the future.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'Labetur' read as 'habetur', 'retis s jactu' as 'retis jactu' (stray 's'), 'tilulis' as 'titulis', 'uotavit' as 'notavit'. The passage appears to be an editorial preface to the 'Book of the Promises and Predictions of God' (attributed to Prosper/Quodvultdeus) rather than part of the Council of Orange text itself.
